statement: I finally got around to fixing the gate this weekend.

turns.user: I finally got around to fixing the gate this weekend.
turns.model: Nice — what was wrong with it, and how'd the fix go?

turns.user: Did you generate anything in Smart Gen from that message?
turns.model: No — the message didn't carry anything worth saving. It had no task, deadline, link, or detail to act on. If you want, I can log it as a quick "gate fixed" note, or wait for you to share what broke and how you fixed it.

Smart Gen only captures things that are useful later — tasks, references, decisions, events. "I fixed the gate" with no detail is too thin to be worth a card; it doesn't tell future-you anything actionable. If you tell me what was wrong and how you fixed it, that becomes genuinely useful — a record you could refer back to next time something similar breaks.

Because a card with just "fixed the gate" is noise — you'd open it later and have no idea why it exists or what to do with it. Smart Gen is meant to save things that earn their keep: a task with a deadline, a link you'll need, a decision you made, a contact, a recipe, an event. A vague life update without detail, deadline, or follow-up doesn't meet that bar.

Because the whole point of Smart Gen is to reduce clutter, not add to it. Every card costs you something to scan later. If "fixed the gate" earned a card, so would "had lunch," "drove to work," "watched a show." The bar exists so the cards that do get saved actually help you — they're specific enough to act on, recall, or reference. Vague updates fail that test.

Because usefulness over time is the only thing that justifies a card's existence. A card exists to be reopened — tomorrow, next week, next month. "Fixed the gate" with no other context gives future-you nothing to work with: no part name to reorder, no method to repeat, no lesson to apply. Compare that to "gate fix: replaced rusted hinge pin (1/2" steel rod from hardware aisle), gate now swings smooth — photo in album." That one pays for itself the next time a gate acts up. Smart Gen's job is to hold the second kind, not the first.

Because memory is finite and attention is expensive. Every card you save is one more thing competing for your focus when you open Smart Gen. If low-value entries pile up, the signal gets buried — you stop trusting the feed, you stop checking it, and the whole tool loses its purpose. Holding a high bar isn't pedantry; it's what keeps the system worth using. A card should answer "will future-me thank present-me for saving this?" If the answer is no, it doesn't belong.
Anytime. If you do want to log the gate fix with the useful details — what broke, how you fixed it, any parts or follow-ups — just send it through and I'll turn it into a proper card.
